chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a sick man who confessed at the time of death to a heir for a debt he owed him. He said, 'That is permissible.' I said, 'And if he bequeathed something to an heir?' He said, 'It is permissible.'

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Confession or acknowledgment of a debt
key_terms.عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ: At the time of death (implying the final illness period)

ai.seo_question: Is a debt confession or bequest to an heir valid at the time of death in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a dying person’s confession of debt to an heir is legally valid, resolving potential disputes over self-dealing. He further affirms the permissibility of bequeathing specific assets to an heir, distinguishing it from the general inheritance share. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding financial transactions and testamentary dispositions during the critical period of *marad al-mawt* (death illness).
